solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In line of strikers, spot light-fingered criminal

indicators.note: placed at the front, 'In' says the following spot sits inside the line of strikers

parts.note: a picket line is formed by workers on strike
a pock is a pimple or pustule

explanation.surface: A spotlight picks out a thief lurking among the strikers on the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK(POCK)ET: the spot goes into the middle of the picket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is a thief who steals from people's pockets, needing nimble fingers.

clue.text: Cheek, weighing into Greek characters about diatribe

indicators.note: to weigh into something is to pile into it, so the cheek ends up inside the pair of letters

parts.note: two letters of the Greek alphabet, phi and pi
lip is impudent talk
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone cheeky laying into Greeks with a rant.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheek is set between the two Greek letters, and 'about' adds the abbreviation for circa at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A philippic, named after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon, is a bitter verbal attack.

clue.text: Beast of burden mostly encountered in the Golden State?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
'in' places the shortened word inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: California, the Golden State, is abbreviated Cal
met, cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A pack animal one might rarely meet in California.
explanation.walkthrough: MET loses its T and goes inside CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are used to carry loads across deserts, a classic working animal.

clue.text: Stingy girl doing what 1 ac aims to do

parts.note: a girl's name

parts.words: doing what 1 ac aims to do
parts.note: a pickpocket aims to pinch, that is steal

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted girl behaving like a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' is the pickpocket in the grid, whose business is pinching.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny-pinching describes someone mean with money, unwilling to spend even small sums.

clue.text: Element regularly faked in new music

indicators.note: 'in' puts the chosen letters inside the rearranged word
something new is remade, so the letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Some substance being faked in modern music, an accusation of artificiality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faked' looks like part of the story about music, but it only supplies its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesium is a soft alkali metal, chemical symbol Cs, a chemical element.

clue.text: Fibrous substance produced by English: first out? The opposite

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the opposite of first out is last in

explanation.surface: A wry question about English batting order, as if the first batsman were out.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse both words of 'first out' to get their opposites, last in.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is the stretchy protein found in connective tissue such as skin and arteries.

clue.text: Fighter pilot crossing river in Brazilian state

indicators.note: the pilot straddles the river, so its letters sit on either side of it

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot flying across a river somewhere in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is a state in western Brazil bordering Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: Charge female leaving continent for republic

parts.note: a charge is a cost

indicators.note: when the woman leaves, her letter departs from the continent's name

parts.note: the continent
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman is accused of leaving one continent for a new country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' could be an accusation; here it means a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American republic between Nicaragua and Panama.

clue.text: Call to mind the first lady touring Oklahoma

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all around it, so the lady's letters surround the state

parts.note: Eve, in Genesis the first woman
OK is the postal abbreviation for Oklahoma

explanation.surface: A US President's wife on tour in Oklahoma brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a President's wife; here she is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon a memory or feeling, to bring it into the mind.

clue.text: The writer's servants given quarters of colossal size

parts.note: the writer is I, so the writer's (the writer is) gives I'M
menservants, men
two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: An author's staff given lodgings of huge proportions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like housing but means points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means huge or vast, exactly the sense of colossal dimensions.

clue.text: Noble embracing love poet

indicators.note: one thing embracing another holds it in its arms, inside it

parts.note: short for aristocrat
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An aristocrat hugging a beloved poet.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside ARISTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Ariosto was the Italian Renaissance writer of the epic poem Orlando Furioso.

clue.text: It's immediate in fellow soldiers primarily employed in Intelligence

parts.note: taken as written
a man's name, a fellow
the Territorial Army

indicators.note: 'in' places the chosen letter inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: nous is common sense or wit

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A spy story: comrades suddenly deployed in military intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; 'Intelligence' looks like the spy service but means good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something instantaneous happens at once, with no delay at all; the 'It's' turns the adjective into a description.

clue.text: Part of Scotland originally inspiring Schubert song

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so each of the next two words gives its first letter

parts.note: first letter
first letter
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A Scottish place that first inspired a Schubert song.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for its whisky, part of Scotland.

clue.text: Lacking will, belonging to trial rowing team, we hear

parts.note: part of a test, in test

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the crew is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a racing boat crew of eight rowers

explanation.surface: A rower in a trial crew who shows no willpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking will' sounds like weakness of character but means having made no legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestate describes someone who dies without having made a valid will.

clue.text: Old man or woman heretic securing Irishman as MP?

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the Irishman is held inside the first word

parts.note: either parent, father or mother
a common Irish man's name
a follower of Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: A dissenting elderly figure holding an Irish politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man or woman' reads as two people but is one word for either, mother or father. Arius was a 4th-century priest condemned as a heretic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament sits in parliament, so is a parliamentarian; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Giving in about gin, sadly, drinking fast

indicators.note: what drinks takes something inside itself

parts.note: re means concerning

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: the Christian season of fasting
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a fast by drinking gin, a sad lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is not speed but abstaining from food, the forty days before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Relenting means softening or yielding, abandoning a harsh position.

clue.text: Manic rule oddly expressed in figures

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic regulation strangely set out in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerical means expressed as numbers, and figures are numbers.

clue.text: Infection requiring relief till work appears

parts.note: a common viral infection
relief from pain or distress
to till is to cultivate land, to farm

explanation.surface: A sick worker needs time off until going back to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like 'until' but is the verb to cultivate. Cold Comfort Farm is Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A work is a literary creation, and this is a famous novel parodying rural melodrama.

clue.text: Roam with this writer and that Cockney woman

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
with means and, in addition
'er, her with the H dropped as a Londoner would

explanation.surface: An author wandering about with a London woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops initial H, so her becomes 'er.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly, as a winding river does.

clue.text: Dismissed, sleeps over in S African grazing area

parts.note: a batsman dismissed is out

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: naps are short sleeps

explanation.surface: Someone sent away sleeps overnight somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: An outspan is a place where oxen are unyoked to graze, a South African term from Afrikaans.

clue.text: Beggar is unable to fix one at first

parts.note: to mend is to repair
the Roman numeral for one
can't, cannot

explanation.surface: A beggar who cannot repair one thing at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' tells you the fix-one pair goes before the 'is unable' part.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is one who lives by begging, as did the medieval mendicant friars.

clue.text: Saw second official principally digesting Times

indicators.note: what digests something takes it inside

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
T is time, so times gives two of them

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so only the leading letter is used

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper official taking in the Times, quoting an old saying.
explanation.walkthrough: MO and O together surround TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, and a motto is a short guiding maxim.

clue.text: Motive for returning, avoiding a strong headwind

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards
avoiding means steering clear of, so the letter named is dropped

parts.note: a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: A sailor's reason for heading back: avoiding a fierce headwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse REASON, then take out its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A noser is a dialect or nautical word for a wind blowing straight into one's face.

clue.text: Bath, say, before greeting old cavalryman

parts.note: Bath is a famous English spa town
an informal hello

explanation.surface: Taking a bath before saying hello to an old horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' is capitalised as the first word, hiding that it is the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A spahi was a cavalry soldier of the Ottoman empire or of French colonial North Africa.

clue.text: Caught on TV initially wearing toupee, perhaps

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter
a toupee is one kind of wig

explanation.surface: Someone spotted on television in a hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught on' seems to mean filmed, but it is the phrasal verb for understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British for to realise or understand, to catch on.

clue.text: Dull woman appearing in short film

indicators.note: appearing in a film means being within it, so she sits inside

parts.note: pic is short for picture
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A boring actress in a brief movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' tells you the word for film is a clipped form.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means unimaginative or ordinary, lacking the flair of poetry.

clue.text: Bess's man, heading off for wild party

indicators.note: with its head off, the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Porgy, Bess's partner in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: Bess's husband leaving for a raucous party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like setting out, but it means losing the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a riotous party of unrestrained indulgence.

clue.text: Derrick's advert for a geraniaceous plant

parts.note: a derrick is a type of crane; possessive
a bill is a poster advertisement

explanation.surface: Derrick placing a newspaper ad for a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Derrick looks like a man's name but is a lifting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranesbill is the common name for wild geraniums, members of the Geraniaceae family.
